MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a factor of 45? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 4
   C. 2
   D. 6

2. Which of these is a factor of 12? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 8
   C. 7
   D. 5

3. Which number is written in words as "five thousand, three hundred"? (1 mark)
   A. 5,030
   B. 53,000
   C. 530
   D. 5,300

4. Which of these shows 270 in words? (1 mark)
   A. two hundred and seventy
   B. three hundred and seventy
   C. two hundred and seven
   D. twenty-seven

5. A bus company carried 2,758 passengers on Friday and 3,946 passengers on Saturday. How many passengers is that in the two days? (1 mark)
   A. 6,694 passengers
   B. 5,694 passengers
   C. 6,804 passengers
   D. 6,704 passengers

6. Work out 4,250 − 1,875. (1 mark)
   A. 2,275
   B. 2,385
   C. 2,375
   D. 3,625

7. What is 45 × 20? (1 mark)
   A. 900
   B. 65
   C. 90
   D. 9,000

8. Work out 25 × 16. (1 mark)
   A. 410
   B. 390
   C. 175
   D. 400

9. What is 61 ÷ 7? (1 mark)
   A. 8 remainder 5
   B. 9 remainder 5
   C. 7 remainder 12
   D. 8 remainder 6

10. What is 65 ÷ 5? (1 mark)
   A. 13
   B. 12
   C. 14
   D. 23

11. Dan writes some more fractions. Which of these is an improper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 8/3
   B. 3/8
   C. 1/2
   D. 4 2/3

12. What is 2/5 of 30? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 12
   C. 18
   D. 6

13. What is 1/3 of 24? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 4
   C. 24
   D. 16

14. In the fraction 2/9, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 7
   C. 2
   D. 9

15. In the number 0.74, the digit 4 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tenths
   B. Ones
   C. Hundredths
   D. Tens

16. A matatu carries m passengers. Eight get in and three get out. Which expression shows the number of passengers now? (1 mark)
   A. m − 5
   B. 8m − 3
   C. m + 5
   D. m + 11

17. Change 9 m 5 cm to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 905 cm
   B. 14 cm
   C. 95 cm
   D. 9,050 cm

18. A rope 7 m 20 cm long is cut into 6 equal pieces. How long is each piece? (1 mark)
   A. 7 m 14 cm
   B. 1 m 20 cm
   C. 1 m 30 cm
   D. 2 m 40 cm

19. Which unit is best for measuring the length of a classroom? (1 mark)
   A. Litres
   B. Centimetres only
   C. Metres
   D. Kilograms

20. Rectangle P has 5 rows and 7 columns. Rectangle Q has 6 rows and 6 columns. Which has the bigger area? (1 mark)
   A. Rectangle P
   B. They are equal
   C. It cannot be told
   D. Rectangle Q

21. A cuboid is 8 blocks long, 2 blocks wide and 5 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 88 blocks
   B. 15 blocks
   C. 80 blocks
   D. 16 blocks

22. Why should heavy boxes be stacked at the bottom? (1 mark)
   A. It makes no difference
   B. So that the boxes are hidden
   C. So that the volume increases
   D. So that the stack is stable and does not fall

23. Which is the best way to read the water level on a measuring jug? (1 mark)
   A. Look with your eyes closed
   B. Look at the scale level with the water
   C. Look from high above the jug
   D. Count the number of handles

24. What is 7 1/2 L − 3 3/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 4 L
   B. 3 1/2 L
   C. 3 3/4 L
   D. 4 1/4 L

25. What is 1 1/4 L + 2 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 4 L
   B. 4 1/4 L
   C. 3 3/4 L
   D. 3 1/2 L

26. A dial scale pointer stops halfway between 3 and 4. What is the mass? (1 mark)
   A. 4 kg
   B. 3 1/2 kg
   C. 3 1/4 kg
   D. 3 kg

27. What is 10 kg − 3 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 7 kg
   B. 6 3/4 kg
   C. 6 1/4 kg
   D. 6 1/2 kg

28. How long is a lesson that starts at 9:30 a.m. and ends at 12:10 p.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 3 h 40 min
   B. 2 h 50 min
   C. 2 h 25 min
   D. 2 h 40 min

29. How many hours are in 3 days? (1 mark)
   A. 36 hours
   B. 96 hours
   C. 180 hours
   D. 72 hours

30. One unit costs Ksh 120. What is the cost of 2 packets of maize flour? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 120
   B. Ksh 250
   C. Ksh 122
   D. Ksh 240

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. The raw data for 10 pupils' favourite fruits is: mango, banana, mango, orange, banana, mango, pawpaw, mango, banana, orange. Make a tally table for this data. (4 marks)

32. Name the plane figure of each object: a plate, a floor tile, a door. (3 marks)

33. Change 45/100, 6/100 and 7/10 into decimals. (3 marks)

34. A tanker fills 100 jerrycans of 20 litres each. How many litres is that? (2 marks)

35. Fill in the 3 times table from 3 × 1 to 3 × 10. Describe one pattern you notice. (4 marks)

36. Amina has a 3 L jug of water. She pours 1 1/4 L into a pot and 1/2 L into a cup. How much water is left in the jug? (4 marks)

37. A shop buys 24 boxes of pencils. Each box has 36 pencils. (a) Estimate the number of pencils by rounding to the nearest ten. (b) Work out the exact number of pencils. (5 marks)

38. Estimate 5,382 + 3,617 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. Then find the exact sum. (4 marks)

39. Divide 96 by 3 by dividing the tens first and then the ones. (3 marks)

40. Name three objects in your classroom that have right angles. (3 marks)

41. Ten pupils chose their favourite drink: 4 chose juice, 3 chose milk, 2 chose water and 1 chose tea. Write two facts that you can read from this data. (2 marks)

42. Explain why multiplying by 100 puts two zeros on the end of a whole number. (3 marks)

43. A stack of soda crates has 5 crates along the wall, 4 crates deep and 4 layers high. How many crates are in the stack? (3 marks)

44. Simplify 2a + 5 + 3a + 1 and find its value when a = 4. (4 marks)

45. A dial scale has big marks for each kilogram and three small marks between them. What mass does the first small mark after 3 kg show? Explain. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 9
   45 ÷ 9 = 5 with nothing left over, so 9 is a factor of 45. The others leave a remainder.

2. A — 4
   12 ÷ 4 = 3 with nothing left over, so 4 is a factor of 12. The others leave a remainder.

3. D — 5,300
   five thousand, three hundred: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 5,300.

4. A — two hundred and seventy
   270 = two hundred and seventy. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

5. D — 6,704 passengers
   Add 2,758 + 3,946 = 6,704 passengers.

6. C — 2,375
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 4,250 − 1,875 = 2,375. Check: 2,375 + 1,875 = 4,250.

7. A — 900
   45 × 2 = 90, then × 10 gives 900.

8. D — 400
   25 × 6 = 150 and 25 × 10 = 250. 150 + 250 = 400.

9. A — 8 remainder 5
   7 × 8 = 56 and 61 − 56 = 5. So 61 ÷ 7 = 8 remainder 5. Check: 8 × 7 + 5 = 61.

10. A — 13
   5 × 13 = 65, so 65 ÷ 5 = 13.

11. A — 8/3
   In an improper fraction the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. 8/3 is one whole or more.

12. B — 12
   30 ÷ 5 = 6 and 6 × 2 = 12. So 2/5 of 30 is 12.

13. A — 8
   24 ÷ 3 = 8 and 8 × 1 = 8. So 1/3 of 24 is 8.

14. D — 9
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

15. C — Hundredths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 0.74 the digit 4 is in the hundredths place.

16. C — m + 5
   m + 8 − 3 = m + 5.

17. A — 905 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 9 × 100 = 900, and 900 + 5 = 905. So the answer is 905 cm.

18. B — 1 m 20 cm
   720 ÷ 6 = 120 cm = 1 m 20 cm.

19. C — Metres
   A classroom is several metres long, so metres are the sensible unit.

20. D — Rectangle Q
   P = 5 × 7 = 35 and Q = 6 × 6 = 36. Rectangle Q has the bigger area.

21. C — 80 blocks
   One layer has 8 × 2 = 16 blocks. There are 5 layers, so the volume is 16 × 5 = 80 blocks.

22. D — So that the stack is stable and does not fall
   A stack with heavy boxes at the bottom is more stable and safer.

23. B — Look at the scale level with the water
   Reading level with the water gives the correct mark.

24. C — 3 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 7 1/2 L − 3 3/4 L = 3 3/4 L.

25. C — 3 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 1 1/4 L + 2 1/2 L = 3 3/4 L.

26. B — 3 1/2 kg
   Halfway between 3 kg and 4 kg is 3 1/2 kg.

27. D — 6 1/2 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 10 kg − 3 1/2 kg = 6 1/2 kg.

28. D — 2 h 40 min
   Count on from 9:30 a.m. to 12:10 p.m.. The total is 2 h 40 min.

29. D — 72 hours
   1 day = 24 hours, so 3 × 24 = 72 hours.

30. D — Ksh 240
   Cost = number × price = 2 × 120 = Ksh 240.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mango 4 (||||), banana 3 (|||), orange 2 (||), pawpaw 1 (|); total 10.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct count of two fruits (2 marks), 1 mark for correct tally marks, 1 mark for the total 10.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plate: circle. Floor tile: square. Door: rectangle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct shape.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.45, 0.06 and 0.7
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct decimal.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: 2,000 litres
   Working / marking points: 20 × 100 = 2,000. 1 mark for the multiplication and 1 mark for units.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30. Each product is 3 more than the one before it (or the products alternate odd and even).
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the table (1 mark if one or two errors), 2 marks for a correct pattern with a reason.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: 1 1/4 L
   Working / marking points: 1 1/4 + 1/2 = 1 3/4 L used (2 marks); 3 − 1 3/4 = 1 1/4 L (2 marks).

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 20 × 40 = 800 (b) 864 pencils
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for 800, 2 marks for 36 × 4 = 144 and 36 × 20 = 720, 1 mark for 864.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 5,380 + 3,620 = 9,000. Exact: 8,999.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rounded number, 1 mark for the estimate 9,000, 1 mark for the exact sum 8,999.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: 32
   Working / marking points: 9 tens ÷ 3 = 3 tens (1 mark); 6 ones ÷ 3 = 2 ones (1 mark); answer 32 (1 mark).

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct, for example a window, a door and a book.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct object.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: juice is the most popular with 4 pupils; only 1 pupil chose tea; 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 pupils were asked.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fact based on the numbers.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each digit moves two places to the left, so it becomes 100 times bigger. The empty tens and ones places are filled with zeros.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for digits moving two places, 1 mark for 100 times bigger, 1 mark for zeros filling places.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 80 crates
   Working / marking points: 5 × 4 = 20 per layer (1 mark); 20 × 4 (1 mark); 80 crates (1 mark).

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: 5a + 6. When a = 4, 5 × 4 + 6 = 26.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 5a, 1 mark for 6, 1 mark for replacing a, 1 mark for 26.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/4 kg. The three small marks divide each kilogram into four equal parts of 1/4 kg.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 3 1/4 kg, 1 mark for four equal parts, 1 mark for 1/4 kg each.
